thesis: Q3 FY26 results (Aug 27, confirmed) beat on EPS ($3.91 vs $3.67 est.) and revenue (+42% YoY to $2.48B), with EDA/Ansys strength driving a raised FY26 outlook (revenue to $9.69-9.74B, EPS to $15.04-15.10) and one analyst calling the print validation that 'AI is a tailwind to EDA/simulation software, rather than a headwind.' Despite that, SNPS is down ~11% net over the past 60 days, and today's -5.4% drop was explicitly framed by market coverage as part of a broad, macro-driven de-rating of high-multiple software/EDA names tied to rising Fed rate-hike odds after a hot August jobs report -- not a company-specific deterioration. Counter-case: the stock's elevated ~74x P/E leaves it vulnerable to further multiple compression if rates keep climbing, and the earnings beat alone doesn't resolve that macro risk.
invalidation: Q4 FY26 results miss the newly raised guidance, or EDA/Ansys growth decelerates independent of the rate backdrop, undercutting the 'pullback is macro, not fundamental' read.

thesis: CN reported record August grain movement (2.50M metric tonnes, confirmed via Sep 3 press release), beating the prior August record of 2.34M MT set in 2020, on the heels of an all-time-high 2025-26 crop year (33.8M MT) and progress on a hybrid-locomotive efficiency pilot (up to 50% fuel savings). These are specific, already-disclosed operational results, not guidance or rumor, and the stock's volume spiked to ~4.3x its 30-day average around this news. Counter-case: grain strength is seasonal and concentrated in one commodity line, so it doesn't by itself confirm trends across CN's other freight segments (intermodal, petroleum & chemicals, metals); this run's research doesn't have segment-level data to rule that out.
invalidation: Subsequent monthly volume data shows grain strength was a one-off not carried into other freight categories, or a broader North American freight slowdown offsets the grain tailwind.

invalidation: Q3 results come in at or below the low end of the guided range, or the memory/semis sector rally reverses sharply, exposing how much of the move was sector-beta rather than company-specific.
